title: feat(mobile): scan addresses from the header QR scanner and unify on-lens scan errors
description:
> Header scan now sends,
> one lens shows every error—
> three scanners aligned.

## What it solves

The mobile header QR scanner only paired WalletConnect codes — scanning an address did nothing. This adds address scanning there (into the Send flow), and unifies how all three QR scanners show scan errors: on the camera lens, not a toast.

## How this PR fixes it

- **Header scanner reads addresses.** `wc:` URIs still pair; a scanned address now routes into `/(send)/recipient` prefilled (like the home Send button); anything else keeps the "Unrecognised QR code" error. Wired via an injected `onAddressScanned` callback so the hook stays navigation-agnostic.
- **Unified on-lens errors.** Shared `ScanErrorOverlay` (message + Try again, dimmed/red lens) replaces the toast in the in-Send and add-account scanners; the camera pauses until Try again.
- **Single-sourced address contract.** `resolveScannedAddress` + the shared message live in `components/Camera/scannedAddress`, consumed by all three scanners.
- **Guarded the new path.** A `handledRef` stops the header address path double-navigating on vision-camera's burst frames (mirrors the existing `pairingRef`).

## How to test it

On mobile, with an active Safe:

1. **Header QR button → Scan QR:** WalletConnect QR pairs; an address QR → Send recipient prefilled; other QR → on-lens "Unrecognised QR code" + Try again.
2. **Home → Send → Scan QR code:** invalid QR → on-lens error + Try again (not a toast); valid address proceeds.
3. **Add existing account → scan:** invalid QR → on-lens error + Try again; valid Safe address → import form.

## Affected flows

- Header scanner — branches `wc:` pair vs. address → Send vs. unrecognised.
- In-Send and add-account scanners — invalid-address error moved to the lens.
- WalletConnect pairing — unchanged (`wc:` still checked first).

## Blast radius

- `useWalletConnectScan` — new optional `onAddressScanned` + `handledRef`; pairing untouched.
- `components/Camera/scannedAddress` (new) — single source of "is this a scannable address", used by all three scanners.
- `components/Camera/ScanErrorOverlay` (new) — shared error UI.
- `useScannedAddressToSend` — chain-mismatch toast + Send navigation, used by Send + header scanners.
- `ImportReadOnly/useScan` — toast → lens error; module-level dedupe + local `ToastViewport` removed (no toast left on that screen).
- No shared `packages/**`, API, feature-flag, route, or persisted-state changes. Mobile-only.

## Risks / not checked

- Not run on a device: `router.replace` from the header modal into the `(send)` stack is verified by reasoning + unit tests only.
- EIP-681 full URIs still unsupported (out of scope, matches prior behavior).
- No analytics impact.

## Visual summary

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph shared["components/Camera (shared)"]
    RSA[resolveScannedAddress]
    SEO[ScanErrorOverlay]
  end

  H["Header scanner"] -->|"wc: URI"| P[Pair WalletConnect]
  H -->|valid address| SEND["Send → recipient (prefilled)"]
  H -->|else| SEO

  S["In-Send scanner"] -->|valid address| SEND
  S -->|invalid| SEO

  I["Add-account scanner"] -->|valid address| IMP[Import account form]
  I -->|invalid| SEO

  H -. uses .-> RSA
  S -. uses .-> RSA
  I -. uses .-> RSA
```

- [x] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊 — none
- [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻
- [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not verify 🎯

findings.claim: Requests restored after an app restart skip the router's signer and chain checks (methodRouter.ts:223-240); the chain check is genuinely missing on the restore path, and the gap could open if a stale-request rejection never reached the dApp before the app was killed, or if the request was only picked up at restart, so a one-line check of chainId against the active chain at line 75 would close it.

The router dispatches on 8 sequential if (method === ...) blocks and the status mapping in services/getCallsStatus.ts:42-43 is a chained ternary, whereas apps/web/docs/code-style.md:47-58 (which mobile follows) says 5 or more conditions should become a lookup table.

The getCallsStatus catch-all converts every failure of transactionsGetTransactionByIdV1, including network errors and 5xx responses, into a generic 'Transaction not found' message, which would cause dApps to misinterpret a temporary outage as an unknown transaction id.

A malformed 'to' value passes the check at this location, leaving the request unanswered until it fails later at services/tx/draft.ts:58 with a generic 'Failed to build transaction' toast, rather than being rejected immediately.
The fallback behavior for a URL that fails to parse is untested.

This commit makes a visible product change (removing the 'This account is only available on …' text, adding a close button, and moving the chain list into a new Supported networks sheet, plus deleting getAvailableChainsNames) but, unlike other commits in the PR, does not cite a Figma design reference in the description.

The new shared stripEip155Prefix function is an exact duplicate of the existing one in apps/web/src/features/walletconnect/services/utils.ts, so web now maintains a parallel copy of logic the shared package owns instead of removing its own copy and re-exporting the package version, as it already does for isPairingUri and getEip155ChainId.

The import reaches directly into @/src/components/Camera/useCameraPermissionFlow instead of using the barrel export at apps/mobile/src/components/Camera/index.ts, which is already used for other Camera imports in the same file, creating inconsistency.

The focus effect unconditionally sets the camera active and resets the scanned flag when the screen regains focus, even if an error overlay is currently shown for an invalid address. This puts a live camera behind the error overlay and can trigger scan logic on a new frame before the user dismisses the overlay, so the effect should be gated on the absence of an error message or the error should be cleared on focus.

review() is only protected against re-entry by the composing state, which disables the button via SafeButton's loading prop after a re-render occurs; a double tap before that re-render can invoke compose twice, triggering two /preview calls, two setOutstandingRequest calls, and two navigations to /confirm-transaction. A synchronous ref-based guard should be added instead.
The call-shape check was copied from web's index.ts:410-422 rather than shared, though it is only about a 10-line predicate.
The NOT_DEPLOYED check inside switchActiveChainByCaip2 is never exercised by a test because every test replaces the function with jest.fn().

Date.now().toString() is used for scanTimestamp, but two rapid taps landing within the same millisecond produce identical values, so the route would not treat them as a new event; a monotonic counter or ref-based increment would be more deterministic.

The test mocks parsePrefixedAddress and isValidAddress transitively even though the hook now calls resolveScannedAddress, coupling the test to internal implementation helpers rather than the actual dependency; mocking @/src/components/Camera/scannedAddress directly would reduce this coupling.

The focus effect unconditionally sets the camera active and resets the scanned flag when the screen regains focus, even if an error overlay is currently shown for an invalid address. This puts a live camera behind the error overlay and can trigger scan logic on a new frame before the user dismisses the overlay, so the effect should be gated on the absence of an error message or the error should be cleared on focus.

This file imports from the deep path @/src/components/Camera/scannedAddress even though the same PR adds a barrel export that the Send and WalletConnect scanners already use, so this caller should use the barrel export too for consistency.

mapTxStatus and buildGetCallsResult duplicate web's BundleTxStatuses and receipts logic instead of sharing it, so the two platforms can drift; web already has a PARTIALLY_REVERTED = 600 status that mobile cannot express, and the code should be moved into the shared packages/utils/src/features/walletconnect/eip5792.ts helper and called from both apps rather than left duplicated (note that this shared helper file is currently used only by mobile, not by both apps as originally claimed).

A fallback setTimeout is created without storing or clearing its reference, so the timer outlives component unmount; it is currently harmless since it only resets a ref, but it is an uncleaned side effect.
The -32602 'Invalid call parameters.' error is constructed inline here, duplicating the private invalidParamsError helper defined in methodRouter.ts; the helper should be exported and reused instead.
ConfirmTx imports WalletConnect-specific components (also at ConfirmTx.container.tsx:20), which conflicts with the feature-import boundary documented in apps/mobile/docs/code-style.md:9.

The component body grew from 121 to 364 lines and now inlines three separate jobs (propose-response listeners at 137-191, rejecting stale requests on a Safe switch at 199-252, and building dependencies for the request handler at 285-391), violating the function-length and single-responsibility limits set in apps/web/docs/code-style.md (applicable to mobile per apps/mobile/AGENTS.md:26); each job should be moved into its own hook, as already done for useSessionRequestHandler and useSendTransaction.
The badge is positioned using raw numeric offsets (top={-10} right={-10}) with no spacing token or comment explaining the values.
shadowColor is set with the hex literal #000 instead of a Tamagui color token, which mobile conventions require; the only other #000 shadow in mobile code is in an e2e test helper.

The getCallsStatus function in the provider is never run by a test; none of its three receipt outcomes (fetched, fetch failed, or no chain config) is covered, only the pure buildGetCallsResult helper is tested.

While review() waits on the composeSafeTxDraft CGW preview call with the request still pending, a chain-switch listener triggered by a second dApp session's wallet_switchEthereumChain call can remove the entry and send the dApp a USER_REJECTED response, after which review() resumes and opens the confirm screen anyway, so a second respondSessionRequest call fails silently and the dApp is told the transaction was rejected even though the Safe transaction is still proposed.
borderRadius values of 10 and 8 are magic numbers with no inline explanation, and the documented exception for unexplained numeric literals only covers 100/150 used for circles.
The spring animation triggered on a value change is never exercised because no test re-renders the component to trigger it.
There is no container test covering the dApp origin and back-rejection wiring.

handledRef is not reset on focus cleanup; it currently only works because the address path unmounts the scanner via router.replace. If a future code path keeps the scanner mounted instead of unmounting it, handledRef staying true would silently suppress all subsequent scans with no indication to the user, so the invariant should be documented with a comment or the ref should be reset in the cleanup.
Scan logic in this file and in Send/ScanQrSend.container.tsx:38-91 is near-identical and duplicated, though with only two copies it may not yet need extracting into a shared implementation.
The composing half of the condition `if (busy || composing) return` has no test covering dismiss-while-building, while the busy half is covered.
The test file is not located next to its source file, which conflicts with the convention documented in AGENTS.md:392.

String(parseInt(target.chainId, 16)) converts malformed hex input such as '0xzz' into the string 'NaN', causing the request to reach switchActiveChainByCaip2('eip155:NaN') and fail with a 4901 'not deployed' error instead of the correct -32602 invalid params error; the hex value should be validated or parsed with BigInt in a try/catch as is already done for wallet_sendCalls, and there is no test covering malformed hex input.
